content: The interaction between ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and other medications can significantly impact drug levels, efficacy, and safety. Below is a detailed explanation of these interactions and recommendations for clinical management: 1. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and vadadustat: Monitor for adverse effects of BCRP substrates and adjust their dose as per product labeling. 2. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and acalabrutinib: Acalabrutinib can increase ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and aluminum hydroxide: Aluminum hydroxide decreases ledipasvir levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. Separate administration of antacids and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by at least 4 hours. 4. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and amiodarone: Co-administration increases the risk of severe bradycardia, which has been associated with death or pacemaker insertion. Patients with cardiac comorbidities or those on beta-blockers are at higher risk. Inpatient cardiac monitoring is recommended for the first 48 hours, followed by outpatient or self-monitoring for 2 weeks. 5. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and apalutamide: Apalutamide decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels by increasing elimination. Monitor closely as apalutamide weakly induces BCRP. 6. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate: These agents decrease ledipasvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Separate administration by 4 hours. 7. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and atorvastatin: Co-administration may increase the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. Monitor closely and consider therapy modification. 8. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and berotralstat: Both drugs increase each other’s levels via P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Monitor closely and adjust P-gp substrate doses if necessary. 9. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and betrixaban: Reduce betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, followed by 40 mg daily if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. Monitor closely. 10. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and calcium carbonate: Calcium carbonate decreases ledipasvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Separate administration by 4 hours. 11. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and carbamazepine: Carbamazepine decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels by inducing P-gp, reducing sofosbuvir’s active metabolite. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and cimetidine: Cimetidine decreases ledipasvir levels by increasing gastric pH. H2-receptor antagonists can be administered simultaneously or 12 hours apart at doses comparable to famotidine 40 mg BID. 13. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and colchicine: Co-administration increases colchicine levels via P-gp inhibition. Avoid use in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If necessary, reduce colchicine dose or frequency. 14. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and dabigatran: Avoid co-administration in atrial fibrillation if CrCl <30 mL/min or in DVT/PE treatment if CrCl <50 mL/min. Monitor closely. 15. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and danicopan: Danicopan increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely and consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates. 16. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and darolutamide: Darolutamide, a BCRP inhibitor, increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels. Avoid co-administration or monitor closely for adverse reactions. 17. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and dexlansoprazole: Dexlansoprazole decreases ledipasvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Proton-pump inhibitors at doses comparable to omeprazole <20 mg can be administered under fasted conditions. 18. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and digoxin: Co-administration increases digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 19. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and duvelisib: Duvelisib increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and edoxaban: Co-administration increases edoxaban levels. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce edoxaban dose to 30 mg daily. No dose reduction is needed for NVAF. Monitor closely. 21. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and elagolix: Elagolix increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely. 22. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases tenofovir levels. Dose adjustment may be necessary. Monitor closely. 23. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and enasidenib: Enasidenib increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via OATP1B1/3 and BCRP inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce substrate dosage. 24. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and encorafenib: Encorafenib, a BCRP inhibitor, increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels. Monitor for toxicity and adjust therapy as needed. 25. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and erdafitinib: Erdafitinib increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp inhibition. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 6 hours. 26. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and esomeprazole: Esomeprazole decreases ledipasvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Proton-pump inhibitors at doses comparable to omeprazole <20 mg can be administered under fasted conditions. 27. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and famotidine: Famotidine decreases ledipasvir levels. H2-receptor antagonists can be administered simultaneously or 12 hours apart at doses comparable to famotidine 40 mg BID. 28. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and fosphenytoin: Fosphenytoin decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and fostamatinib: Fostamatinib increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp/BCRP inhibition. Monitor for toxicities and adjust doses as needed. 30. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and fostemsavir: Fostemsavir inhibits BCRP transporters, increasing ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels. Avoid co-administration or modify substrate doses. 31. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and glecaprevir/pibrentasvir: Co-administration increases plasma concentrations of P-gp and BCRP substrates. Monitor closely. 32. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and ibuprofen/famotidine: Famotidine decreases ledipasvir levels. Administer H2-receptor antagonists simultaneously or 12 hours apart. 33. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and istaroxime: Istaroxime increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely and consider dose reduction. 34. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and lansoprazole: Lansoprazole decreases ledipasvir levels. Proton-pump inhibitors at doses comparable to omeprazole <20 mg can be administered under fasted conditions. 35. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and lasmiditan: Lasmiditan inhibits BCRP, increasing ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels. Avoid co-administration. 36. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and leniolisib: Leniolisib, a BCRP inhibitor, increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels. Avoid co-administration or monitor closely. 37. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and lonafarnib: Lonafarnib, a weak P-gp inhibitor, increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels. Monitor for adverse reactions and reduce P-gp substrate doses if needed. 38. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and magnesium oxide: Magnesium oxide decreases ledipasvir levels. Separate administration by 4 hours. 39. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and mavorixafor: Co-administration increases levels of both drugs via P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust doses as needed. 40. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and momelotinib: Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels. Monitor for adverse reactions and adjust therapy. 41. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and naloxegol: Co-administration increases naloxegol levels. Monitor for adverse effects. 42. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and nintedanib: Co-administration increases nintedanib levels. Manage adverse effects with dose reduction or therapy discontinuation. 43. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and nizatidine: Nizatidine decreases ledipasvir levels. Administer H2-receptor antagonists simultaneously or 12 hours apart. 44. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and omeprazole: Omeprazole decreases ledipasvir levels. Proton-pump inhibitors at doses <20 mg can be administered under fasted conditions. 45. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and otesenol: Otesenol, a BCRP inhibitor, increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or reduce doses. 46. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and oxcarbazepine: Oxcarbazepine decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 47. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and pantoprazole: Pantoprazole decreases ledipasvir levels. Proton-pump inhibitors at doses <20 mg can be administered under fasted conditions. 48. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and phenobarbital: Phenobarbital decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 49. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and phenytoin: Phenytoin decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 50. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and rabeprazole: Rabeprazole decreases ledipasvir levels. Proton-pump inhibitors at doses <20 mg can be administered under fasted conditions. 51. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and regorafenib: Regorafenib inhibits BCRP, increasing ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels. Monitor for toxicity and adjust therapy. 52. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and repotrectinib: Co-administration increases repotrectinib levels. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 53. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and resmetirom: Resmetirom levels increase with co-administration. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 54. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and rifabutin: Rifabutin decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 55. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and rifampin: Rifampin decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 56. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and rifapentine: Rifapentine decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 57. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and rimegepant: Co-administration increases rimegepant levels. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 58. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and rosuvastatin: Co-administration increases the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. Monitor closely. 59. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and safinamide: Safinamide inhibits intestinal BCRP, increasing ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels. Monitor for pharmacologic or adverse effects. 60. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and sarecycline: Sarecycline increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor for toxicities and adjust doses. 61. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and seladelpar: Co-administration increases seladelpar levels. Monitor for adverse effects. 62. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and sodium zirconium cyclosilicate: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate increases gastric pH, decreasing ledipasvir levels. Administer drugs at least 2 hours apart. 63. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and sotorasib: Sotorasib decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp induction. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 64. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 65. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and stiripentol: Stiripentol increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via BCRP inhibition. Monitor for adverse effects and adjust doses. 66. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and tafamidis: Tafamidis inhibits BCRP, increasing ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels. Adjust BCRP substrate doses as needed. 67. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and talazoparib: Co-administration increases talazoparib levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely. 68. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases tenofovir levels. Monitor closely and adjust therapy. 69. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and tepotinib: Tepotinib increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp inhibition. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 70. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and tipranavir: Tipranavir decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 71. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and topotecan: Co-administration increases topotecan levels. Avoid or use alternative therapy.
